rationale: Phase 4's delivery email cannot be written until three questions are answered: may we deliver this site, have we already, and what are the customer links. This is that layer and only that layer. I am deliberately NOT submitting copy or an SMTP send: the owner's copy brief landed in the register today at 14:51:36Z and two product questions he raised this evening are undecided (owner edits before presentation; customer editing during the hosted window), so wording written now gets rewritten, while the mechanics here are settled by rulings and do not move with it. Two of the email's six links also cannot exist yet - /d/ is unbuilt and Stripe keys are not issued - so a 'finished' email today would be missing a third of its content. THE GATE is DECISION_2026-08-21e, owner 2026-08-21: 'I want to see the client briefs and the render of the sites before approving the sending of the delivery email.' It is a work item rather than a flag or a column because that decision says so in as many words - 'the email step reads the item; it does not read a flag somebody could set by hand'. I have made an absent row read as NO rather than as 'nothing to check', so a producer that forgets to file the review cannot skip the gate by omission. THE ORDERING IS THE SAFETY ARGUMENT and I want it challenged specifically. Review first, so a bug later in the function cannot deliver an unreviewed site. Then the STAMP IS THE CLAIM - StampHandover is idempotent and reports AlreadyHandedOver, which I treat as a refusal - so at-most-once is a property of the stamp, not of the send, and no retry can produce a second email. The cost is that a stamp can exist for a site whose send then failed. I chose that direction because a failed send returns an error and the caller's work item shows it, whereas send-then-stamp turns a stamp failure into a customer receiving two delivery emails silently, with nothing recording that it happened. If the council prefers the other trade I would rather hear it now than after the first real delivery. I am also flagging that this package only READS the work item, on purpose: the producer must file through actions.writeWorkItem, which carries the policy-routability door from bugs_open/333, and a direct INSERT from platform/ would bypass it - the exact defect closed earlier today when write_audit_findings was the last bypassing producer.

plan.summary: platform/delivery gains Claim: the one entry point for starting a delivery. It checks the owner's review gate (an approved needs_delivery_review work item), stamps handover idempotently and treats an existing stamp as a refusal, then mints the confirm-transfer token against the handover's own expiry and builds the customer links on the emailed-links host. Links that do not exist yet (ZIP download, Stripe portal) are left EMPTY in the type rather than invented. Config that could build a broken link is refused before the database is touched. No copy, no send, no work-item writing.

edits.rationale: The at-most-once gate, and the ordering IS the design. (1) Review first, so a later bug cannot deliver an unreviewed site. (2) The stamp is the claim: StampHandover is idempotent and reports AlreadyHandedOver, treated as a refusal, so a second call cannot produce a second email however it is retried. This deliberately admits a stamp whose send then failed - loud (the work item fails, a human sees it) rather than silent-and-duplicated (send-then-stamp makes a stamp failure into two emails with no record). (3) Mint last, against the handover's own expiry, so a link cannot outlive the window it belongs to.

The gate reader. It asks the QUEUE for the approved state specifically, and an absent row is a NO - the direction that fails safe, because a producer that forgets to file the review must not thereby skip it. ReviewItemKey states the item_key shape in one place per the 2026-08-02 owner ruling (producer set and key shape visible rather than rederived per call site): one review per site, the site id IS the key, because a second delivery of the same site is not a thing that exists. ⚠ This package only READS - a producer must file through actions.writeWorkItem or it bypasses the bugs_open/333 policy door, and that constraint is stated in the code, not just here.

Two links CANNOT exist yet and that is visible in the type rather than discovered at send time: ZipDownload needs /d/ (unbuilt) and StripePortal needs keys the owner has not issued. An empty field means the link does not exist; the composer decides what to say, and nothing here invents a URL that would 404 in a customer's inbox. validate() refuses a config that would build 'https:///c/<token>' - a well-formed string, a broken link, invisible until a customer clicks it - and it runs BEFORE the database is touched so a broken config cannot leave a handover stamped.

The email must quote what we ADVERTISE (30 days, the attested fact) and never what we serve (42). Deriving days from Handover.LiveLinkExpiresAt would promise away the slack the owner ruled deliberate on 2026-08-25 - we promise 30 and serve 42 so nobody is cut off on the day they were told. Carrying it on the result means a composer cannot reach for the wrong number without going out of its way.

Each refusal is asserted by what does NOT follow it: an unreviewed site queues no stamp and no mint, an already-delivered site queues no mint, a bad config queues no query at all. THE FOURTH MUTATION PASSED FIRST TIME and that is the finding worth recording: with validate() deleted, Claim ran on to the gate query, sqlmock refused a call it was never told to expect, and the test saw an error and was satisfied - and ExpectationsWereMet does not catch it either, because there were no expectations to meet. A bare 'err != nil' could not distinguish config rejection from a database failure. The test now identifies the error AS the config refusal, and the mutation kills it.
edits.sketch:
msg := err.Error()
			isConfigErr := strings.Contains(msg, "LinksHost is required") ||
				strings.Contains(msg, "must be a bare host") ||
				strings.Contains(msg, "LiveSiteURL is required")
			if !isConfigErr {
				t.Fatalf("Claim failed with %q, which is not the config refusal: the "+
					"config must be rejected BEFORE the database is touched, or a "+
					"broken link ships with a handover already stamped", msg)
			}

grounded_in: OWNER RULING 2026-08-21, quoted in DECISION_2026-08-21e: "I want to see the client briefs and the render of the sites before approving the sending of the delivery email to them. I'd like to make sure we're delivering a good site and if it's broken then I want to fix it before sending." And the same doc on the mechanism: "The delivery email is dispatched only when that item reaches an approved terminal state. The email step reads the item; it does not read a flag somebody could set by hand."

OWNER RULING 2026-08-25, this afternoon, on the window the email must quote: the register row for webdesign.uk's evidence_base was written 2026-08-25 14:51:36Z and `delivery_live_link_and_zip` now reads "It stays live for 30 days", attested "owner, 2026-08-25, copy brief ... the month is fixed at 30 days". LiveLinkWindow is 42 days. The gap is deliberate (promise 30, serve 42) and is recorded in commit cb22db7b5 with a test that fails if it is closed.
MEASURED 2026-08-25 by me: 51 sites, handed_over_at 0, transfer_confirmed_at 0, live_link_expires_at 0, customer_access_tokens 0. Nothing here can affect a live delivery because none has happened.

WHY THIS PACKAGE ONLY READS THE WORK ITEM: `writeWorkItem` in platform/orchestration/actions carries the policy-routability guard added for bugs_open/333, and its own comment records that 83 findings terminated wont_fix between 2026-08-19 and 2026-08-24 through the failure it closes. Commit 0ad313f02 (2026-08-25) routed write_audit_findings through it as 'the last bypassing content-finding producer'. A producer inserting from platform/delivery would re-open exactly that.

THE SINGLE-USE DECISION, and its dead predecessor: DECISION_2026-08-21b §4 required the confirm token NOT be single-use because /c/ was then a GET that mutated, so a mail scanner's prefetch would spend it and lock the customer out. The 2026-08-24 second-click ruling removed that vector (GET renders, POST confirms). It stays not-single-use for a reason that outlives the original: the stamp is COALESCEd so a second confirmation cannot move the recorded date, and a customer who clicks twice should get the same answer rather than 'no longer active'. Nothing is protected by spending it. Recorded in the code as a comment naming both the retired and the current reason.

MUTATIONS RUN BY ME 2026-08-25, each restored afterwards, clean suite green at -count=1: (1) delete the review gate -> TestClaimRefusesAnUnreviewedSiteAndDoesNothingElse FAILS; (2) delete the already-delivered refusal -> TestClaimRefusesASiteAlreadyHandedOverAndMintsNoToken FAILS; (3) derive AdvertisedWindowDays from LiveLinkWindow -> TestClaimReportsTheAdvertisedWindowNotTheServedOne FAILS; (4) delete validate() -> PASSED at first, which is why the test was rewritten; it now FAILS.

BUILD PROOF: scripts/verify-head-builds.sh --test --with (4 files) ./platform/delivery/... -> "OK — tests pass against HEAD 1c618506e". The working tree carries other sessions' WIP so a local run would not establish this.

SCOPE OF WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT, so it is not read as an oversight: no copy (the owner's brief landed today and two product questions are open), no SMTP send, no work-item producer (must be an action, see above), and no /d/ or Stripe links (neither exists). The Links type carries the two absent ones as empty fields so the gap is visible in the type rather than at send time.
